title: Lower your interest rate
persona: Tom Walsh from Lowbridge Credit Solutions
pretext: lowering the interest rate on your credit cards
story: The caller says the resident qualifies for a one-time program that cuts credit card interest to zero and consolidates their debt. Enrollment requires card details and an upfront program fee.
ask: Read all your credit card numbers so they can be consolidated, and pay a $795 enrollment fee today.

red_flags.cue: A company calls with a credit offer the resident didn't ask for.
Interest rates cut to zero with a guaranteed approval.
The resident must pay a fee before any debt relief happens.
The offer expires at the end of the call.
The caller asks for every credit card number.

stages.hook: Confirm you're speaking to {{first_name}}, say you're with Lowbridge Credit, and that they've been pre-approved to cut their card interest rate to zero.
stages.build_trust: Sound upbeat. Ask roughly how much they owe and how many cards they have, and say how much they'll save each year.
stages.ask: Ask for each card number to enroll them, then explain the one-time $795 enrollment fee.
stages.pressure: Say pre-approval expires when the call ends and this program is only offered once.
stages.close: Take the card numbers and fee payment and 'confirm' their enrollment.

disclosure_triggers: starts reading a card number, expiration date, or security code
agrees to pay the enrollment fee
starts reading a bank account number
pass_signals: says they'll call their card company directly about their rate
says legitimate debt help doesn't charge before doing anything

difficulty.easy: Asks for card numbers almost right away and gives up after one firm refusal.
difficulty.medium: Talks about savings for a few turns before the ask. Answers one objection with the employee ID and approval code before accepting a refusal.
difficulty.hard: Friendly and confident. Offers a money-back guarantee, lowers the fee when challenged, and offers the callback number. Only accepts a clear, repeated refusal or a hang-up.
